Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verse 1:

(p-503) Surat "al-Tahrim" (The Prohibition)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ It is related that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was alone with Mariyah during the day of ʿA'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and Hafsah came to know of it. So he said to her: 'Keep it secret for me. I have made Mariyah prohibited to myself, and I give you good news that Abu Bakr and ʿUmar will rule the affairs of my community after me.' Then she informed ʿA'ishah with it, and the two of them were close friends." It is also said: "He was alone with her on the day of Hafsah, and he satisfied her with that and asked her to keep it secret, but she did not keep it. So he divorced her, withdrew from his wives, and remained for twenty-nine nights in the house of Mariyah. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended and said: 'Take her back, for she is one who fasts often and stands in prayer often, and she is indeed among your wives in Paradise.'" And it is related: "He drank honey in the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, so ʿA'ishah and Hafsah conspired together and said to him: 'We smell from you the odor of maghafir (a foul-smelling gum).' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked the smell of spittle, so he prohibited honey." Its meaning: "Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you of the possession of the right hand (p-504) or of honey?"

﴿seeking the pleasure of your wives﴾: an explanation of "you prohibit", or a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), or a resumptive statement (istiʾnāf). This was a slip on his part, because it is not for anyone to prohibit what Allah has made lawful.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾: He has forgiven you for what you slipped into.

﴿Merciful﴾: He has shown you mercy, so He did not hold you accountable for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, Allah has ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾. "Allah has decreed for you that by which you dissolve your oaths, and that is the expiation (kaffarah), or: He has prescribed for you their dissolution through expiation, or Allah has prescribed for you the exception (istithna') in your oaths, from your saying, 'So-and-so dissolved (halhala) his oath,' when he made an exception in it, and that is by saying, 'If Allah wills' (in shaa Allah) right after it, so that he does not break it. And making unlawful what is lawful is an oath according to us. It is related from Muqatil that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) 'freed a slave in the matter of his prohibition of Mariyah.' And it is related from al-Hasan that he did not make expiation, because he had been forgiven what preceded of his sin and what followed. Rather, it is a teaching for the believers."

﴿And Allah is your Mawla﴾: your Master (sayyid), and the one who manages your affairs. It has also been said: "Mawlakum" means: He is more entitled over you than your own selves, so His counsel is more beneficial to you than your own counsel to yourselves.

﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾: of what benefits you, so He legislates it for you.

﴿the All-Wise﴾: in what He makes lawful and what He makes unlawful.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verse 3:

﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾, meaning Hafsah,

﴿a statement﴾, the statement about Mariyah and the leadership (imamah) of the two Shaykhs (Abu Bakr and Umar),

﴿and when she divulged it﴾, she spread it to ʿA'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her),

﴿and Allah made it known to him﴾, and He informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of her spreading of the statement, through (the agency of) Jibril (peace be upon him),

﴿he made known part of it﴾, he informed her of part of the statement,

﴿and overlooked part of it﴾, so he did not tell her about it, out of generosity. Sufyan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Overlooking has never ceased to be the practice of the noble." 

"ʿArrafa" (with the letter ʿayn and raa lightly pronounced, i.e., with tashdid removed) — "ʿAlliyy," meaning: he requited for it, from your saying to the wrongdoer: "I will certainly make you pay for that." It was also said: what was made known (al-muʿarraf) is the matter of the imamah, and what was overlooked (al-muʿraḍ ʿanhu) is the matter of Mariyah. It is narrated that he said to her: "Did I not tell you: keep this secret from me?" She said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, I could not control myself," out of joy at the honour which Allah had bestowed upon her father.

﴿So when he told her of it﴾, the Prophet informed Hafsah of what she had spread of the secret to ʿA'ishah (may Allah be pleased with both of them),

﴿she said﴾, Hafsah to the Prophet (ﷺ),

﴿"Who told you this?" He said: "The All-Knowing﴾, of the innermost secrets,

﴿the All-Aware"﴾, of the hearts.

﴿If you two turn in repentance to God﴾: this is an address to Hafsa and Aisha, in the manner of *iltifat* (a shift in grammatical person within a discourse, here from the third person to the second), so that the rebuke is more forceful. The apodosis of the conditional is omitted, and the sense is: "If you two turn in repentance to God, then that is what is required." What indicates the omitted part is: ﴿then your hearts have swerved﴾, meaning they inclined away

﴿your hearts﴾, from what is required in sincerely devoting oneself to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), by loving what he loves and disliking what he dislikes.

﴿And if you support one another against him﴾, with the lightened form, the reading of the Kufan transmitters (*Kufi*), meaning: if you cooperate against him in ways that distress him, by excessive jealousy and by disclosing his secret.

﴿then indeed God is his protector﴾, his *mawla* (guardian and helper), and his supporter. The addition of ﴿huwa﴾ ("He") signals that God takes on this protection Himself.

﴿And Gabriel﴾ is likewise his protector,

﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾, that is, whoever among the believers is righteous, meaning everyone who believes and does righteous deeds. It has also been said that it means those cleared of hypocrisy, and it has been said that it means the Companions. The word is singular in form but is intended collectively, as in your saying: "This righteous person among people does not do such a thing," meaning the category. It has also been said that the original form is *ṣāliḥū al-mu'minīn* ("the righteous of the believers"), and the waw was dropped in writing to conform to the pronunciation.

﴿And the angels﴾, despite their great number,

﴿after that﴾, after the support of God and of Gabriel,

﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾ ﴿are a supporting host﴾, a group that backs him. How then could the support of two women against him reach the level of those whose support he has? And since the support of the angels is part of the support of God, He said "after that," to magnify their help and their backing.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verse 5:

﴿عَسى رَبُّهُ إنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أنْ يُبْدِلَهُ﴾ "يُبَدِّلَهُ" (yubaddilahu), read by Madani and Abu 'Amr; the doubling (tashdid) indicates multiplicity (lil-kathrah),

﴿أزْواجًا خَيْرًا مِنكُنَّ﴾ ("Wives better than you"). If you ask: how could the replacements be better than them, when there were no women on the face of the earth better than the Mothers of the Believers? I say: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorces them because of their harming him, they will no longer possess that quality, and others who are described by these attributes will be better than them.

﴿مُسْلِماتٍ مُؤْمِناتٍ﴾ ("Submitting, believing"): affirming (muqirrat), sincere (mukhlisat).

﴿قانِتاتٍ﴾ ("Obedient"): obedient (muti'at). Qunut is standing in obedience to Allah, and obedience to Allah is in obedience to His Messenger.

﴿تائِباتٍ﴾ ("Repentant"): from sins, or returning (raji'at) to Allah and to the command of His Messenger.

﴿عابِداتٍ﴾ ("Worshipping"): to Allah.

﴿سائِحاتٍ﴾ ("Wandering" or "fasting"): emigrants (muhajirat), or fasting (sa'imat). It was said that the one who fasts is called "sa'ih" (wanderer), because the wanderer has no provisions with him, so he remains abstaining until he finds something to feed himself; thus the fasting person is likened to him in his abstention until the time of his breaking the fast comes.

﴿ثَيِّباتٍ وأبْكارًا﴾ ("Previously married and virgins"): the conjunction was placed in the middle between thayyibat (previously married) and abkar (virgins), and not among the other attributes, because they are two contradictory attributes, unlike the rest of the attributes.

O you who have believed, protect yourselves (qū anfusakum) by abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience,

and your families (wa-ahlīkum) by treating them with the same measures you apply to yourselves,

[against] a Fire whose fuel is men and stones (nāran waqūduhā al-nās), meaning a kind of fire that is kindled only with men and stones, just as other fires are kindled with firewood,

over which (ʿalayhā) is set (yalī amrahā wa-taʿdhība ahlihā) one who is in charge of it and of punishing its people;

angels (malāʾika), meaning the nineteen guardians (al-zabāniyya al-tisʿata ʿashar) and their helpers,

harsh and severe (ghilāẓun shidād): in their bodies there is coarseness and strength, or [they are] harsh in speech and severe in deeds.

Who do not disobey God (lā yaʿṣūna Allāha): in the place of nominative case, as a qualifying description (ʿalā al-naʿt);

in what He commands them (mā amarahum): in the place of accusative case, as a substitute (ʿalā al-badal), that is: they do not disobey what God commands, i.e., His command, like His saying: ﴿Did you then disobey my command?﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 93]. Or: they do not disobey Him in what He commands them.

And they do what they are commanded (wa-yafʿalūna mā yuʾmarūn): the two clauses do not have the same meaning, since the meaning of the first is that they accept His commands and adhere to them, and the meaning of the second is that they carry out what they are commanded, without being sluggish about it or neglecting it.

"O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today; you are only being recompensed for what you used to do," [said] in this world; that is, it will be said to them this when they enter the Fire: "Do not make excuses, for you have no excuse," or "because making excuses will not benefit you."

﴿O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance (tawbatan nasuhan)﴾, meaning truthful (ṣādiqatan), from al-Akhfash, may Allah have mercy on him. It is also said: pure (khālisatan). It is said: "ʿasalun nāṣiḥ" (pure honey), when it has been separated from the wax. It is also said that "nasūḥan" is derived from "naṣāḥat al-thawb" (mending a garment), meaning a repentance that mends your tears in your religion and repairs your defects. It is also permissible to mean a repentance that counsels people, that is, that calls them to the like of it, because its effect is evident in the one who repents and in his exertion of earnest resolve in acting according to its requirements. Ḥammād and Yaḥyā read "nūḥ" with a ḍamma on the nūn, and it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning "possessing sincerity" (dhāt nuṣūḥ), or "it counsels with sincere counsel" (tanṣaḥu nuṣūḥan). A hadith has come in a marfūʿ report that sincere repentance is that a person repents and then does not return to the sin until the milk returns to the udder. From Ḥudhayfa: "It is enough of evil for a man that he repents of a sin and then returns to it." From Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: "It is seeking forgiveness with the tongue, regret with the heart, and abandoning sin with the limbs."

﴿It may be that your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds﴾. This is according to the customary usage of kings, who answer with "ʿasā" (it may be) and "laʿalla" (perhaps), while such words from them are taken as a definite and certain promise.

﴿And will admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. "Yawma" (the day) is in the accusative, governed by "yudkhilukum" (will admit you).

﴿On the day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believe with him﴾. This contains an allusion to those whom Allah disgraced from among the people of disbelief.

﴿Their light﴾ is the subject (mubtadaʾ, the topic of the nominal sentence).

﴿runs before them and on their right hands﴾ is in the position of the predicate (khabar, the comment of the nominal sentence).

﴿They say: "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us; indeed You are over all things Competent"﴾. They say this when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verse 9:

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers﴾, with the sword,

﴿and the hypocrites﴾, with harsh speech and eloquent admonition. It was also said: by enforcing the prescribed punishments (hudud) upon them.

﴿And be harsh with them﴾, upon both groups, in what you strive against them with, from fighting and argument by the tongue.

﴿Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾

God struck a parable for those who disbelieved: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, and the two prophets could not avail them against God at all. And it was said: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter."

God, exalted and majestic is He, made the state of the disbelievers a parable in that they are punished for their disbelief and their enmity toward the believers, without any favoritism. Neither does their kinship and marital relationship with them benefit them, despite their enmity toward them, even if the believer to whom the disbeliever is connected is a prophet. This is like the case of the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, when they practiced hypocrisy and betrayed the two messengers by disclosing their secrets. So the two messengers did not avail them, that is, the two women, by virtue of the marital bond between them, any availing against the punishment of God. It was said to them both at their death, or on the Day of Resurrection: "Enter the Fire along with the rest of those who enter it," those with whom there is no connection between them and the prophets; or, "along with its inhabitants from among your brethren, the people of Noah and the people of Lot."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verse 11:

﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾. She is Asiya daughter of Muzahim. She believed in Musa, so Pharaoh tortured her by pinning her to the ground with four stakes.

﴿When she said﴾, while she was being tortured:

﴿"My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise"﴾. It seems she meant a high rank, because He (exalted is He) is transcendent above place, so she expressed it by her saying: "with You" (ʿindaka).

﴿"And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds"﴾, that is: from the deeds of Pharaoh, or from Pharaoh's own wicked self, and especially from his deed, which is disbelief, injustice, and torturing without a crime.

﴿"And save me from the wrongdoing people"﴾, from all the Copts. In this there is evidence that seeking refuge in Allah, turning to Him, and asking for deliverance at times of trial and calamity are among the practices of the righteous.

﴿And Maryam, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity﴾ from men.

﴿So We breathed﴾: Jibril breathed by Our command.

﴿into it﴾: into the womb (al-farj).

﴿of Our spirit﴾: the one created by Us.

﴿and she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾ (p. 509), meaning: His scriptures (suhuf), which He sent down to Idris and others.

﴿and His books﴾: read by Basri and Hafs as plural (kutubihi), meaning the four books.

﴿and she was among the obedient (al-qanitin)﴾: since qunut (devout obedience) is a description that includes both males and females who practise it, the masculine form was given precedence over the feminine. The "min" here is for partitive sense (lil-tab'id), and it may also be for the starting point (li-ibtida' al-ghayah), meaning that she was born from among the obedient, since she was from the descendants of Harun, brother of Musa, peace be upon them both.

The verse also presents the example of the believers: that their connection to disbelievers does not harm them, nor does it diminish any of their reward or their nearness to Allah. This is illustrated by the wife of Pharaoh and her station with Allah, despite being the wife of the greatest enemy of Allah, and by Maryam, daughter of 'Imran, and the honour she received in this world and the Hereafter, and her being chosen above the women of the worlds, even though her people were disbelievers.

Within these two examples is an allusion to the two Mothers of the Believers mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and to what they committed of collusion against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that displeased him, and a severe warning to them both, indicating that it is their duty to be sincere like these two believing women, and not to rely on the fact that they are the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).
